findings.title: Login-cache invalidation treats wrapped isEnabled() as the DB flag
findings.body: update() loads the previous identity provider with getById() and passes that instance to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(). With the organization feature on, getById() does not return the persisted row; it returns the wrapper from createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(), whose isEnabled() is false whenever the IdP has an organization id and the organization is missing, the organization is disabled, or OrganizationProvider.isEnabled() is false, even if the IdP's own enabled flag is still true. The new login list is populated by idpDelegate.getForLogin(), which filters on the stored enabled, link-only, hide-on-login, and kc.org.broker.public values, not on that wrapper. getLoginPredicate() calls IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled, so on the wrapper it can conclude the IdP was never a login IdP. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then returns without invalidating realmId.idp.login.* when the update model also fails the predicate — for example the update sets hideOnLogin, linkOnly, enabled=false, or clears kc.org.broker.public, which is exactly when the cached id list must be dropped. A common admin sequence hits this: organizations (or one org) are disabled, a public login IdP is edited so it should disappear from getForLogin, then organizations are turned back on. getForLogin still expands the cached internal ids and does not re-apply the login filters, so it returns an IdP the JPA query would exclude. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login, link-only, or broker-public, so the login page will show a broker the admin hid or marked non-public. Decide invalidation from the raw persisted model (idpDelegate.getById), not the organization-aware wrapper. The new OrganizationCacheTest only updates IdPs while they remain effectively enabled, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Login-cache test deletes the alias "alias" instead of the IdPs it creates
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove, both in the creation loop (line 381) and again for idp-alias-20 (line 425). That is the literal alias "alias", not idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-20. Cleanup therefore issues a delete for a provider that was never created and leaves the new brokers in the shared test realm, including enabled, non-hidden realm IdPs and public organization brokers. The same mistake is already present in testCacheIDPByOrg (line 303), which creates org-idp-0..org-idp-9, sets kc.org.broker.public=true, and links them to organizations. If that method runs first, those brokers are still present when this test calls getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, orgaId), so the expected sizes 5 and 10 are wrong and the new test fails. Even if this test runs first, the leaked idp-alias-* providers remain for later organization and broker tests. Capture the real alias in a final variable and register cleanup against that resource.
